text:
elaine: FYI — I'm putting up a proposal to tighten Console access surface. Plan is to split the old 'viewer' into two distinct roles (viewer + read-only-analytics) so we can hide billing/export UI and limit API key export paths. Draft PR: https://git/repo/PR-4521 :eyes:

raj: paste the mapping table? is this just UI gating or are we changing authZ checks too?

elaine: both. backend will introduce explicit permissions: 'project.view', 'project.read_analytics', 'project.manage'. UI will gate billing/usage widgets on 'project.read_analytics'. We'll also migrate legacy role bindings -> new permission set.

brian: heads-up — session tokens pre-migration may carry legacy claims. we need a plan to avoid stale JWTs granting more access after migration. token invalidation or a claim versioning approach required. :thinking_face:

marta: audit requirements: log the migration as an explicit event type (rbac.migration) with actor, before/after, and KMS key id used when we encrypt role blobs. also log UI gating decisions (e.g., why billing widget was hidden) for compliance.

security-bot: Alert: previous rule CVE-2024-XXXX noted a UI leak where billing widget was visible when feature flags desynced. recommend server-side enforcement for billing endpoints.

elaine: Agreed. UI gating only for UX. server must always check 'project.read_analytics' before returning billing/export data. Plan: add middleware check + migration that bumps role_version claim and triggers token refresh.

raj: invalidate tokens = force logout all sessions? heavy for customers. alternative: introduce role_version in JWT and make middleware require token.role_version >= user.role_version. then we can roll migration per-account and let clients refresh.

brian: +1 to role_version. For Dedicated/Private customers we should provide a migration marker they can opt into and a CLI to rotate local session caches. also need doc for SSO providers (okta, azure) — claims mapping will change.

marta: For audit stream, also include a one-time 'rbac.migration_marker' entry per org with KMS-wrapped metadata. That gives us non-repudiable evidence of who ran the migration and which key id protected bindings.

elaine: I'll open the PR with the mapping table and a middleware prototype. quick reviewers: @raj @brian for KMS + token flow. ETA: EOW for staging rollout. @security-bot can you add a monitor for 403 spikes during rollout?

security-bot: Monitor created: rule=rbc_migration_403_spike, trigger=5% increase in 403s over 10m, notify=#incidents and paging on-call.

brian: Reviewing PR tomorrow. small nit: include migration dry-run mode that emits audit events but doesn't modify bindings so we can validate impact.

elaine: Good call — adding dry-run. will also include sample curl and a snippet for role_version claim to share with SDK teams:

```
# sample JWT claim check (middleware)
if token.role_version < user.role_version:
  return 401 "stale-session: please refresh token"
```

elaine: Any other blockers?

raj: Need signoff from legal for storing KMS key id in logs for EU customers. check GDPR data minimization. i'll loop in legal.

marta: I'll draft the audit-schema PR and include retention policy notes.

elaine: Awesome — thanks all. will post PR link here when ready. :rocket:
